content.text:
**Finding: missing (high severity) — no Customer termination for convenience.**

- Section 9 contains only cause-based exits: material breach (9.1), insolvency (9.2), and security/service-failure (9.3). There is no 9.4; the section jumps to 9.5. Other termination hooks (6.2, 19.4, 27.3) are all cause-based.
- The term is three years (8.1), and Section 2.1 layers a USD 2,000,000/year take-or-pay commitment "without reduction or termination rights" — expressly negating any exit.
- That is walk-away territory under T4C (no Customer convenience right in a multi-year term), so it fails the fallback rather than sitting at it.
- Vendor has no convenience right, so nothing needs to be deleted on that side.

Redline (validated, preferred position): new Section 9.4 giving Customer convenience termination on 30 days' notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees and confirming Vendor has no convenience right during a committed term, plus a minimal conforming edit to Section 2.1 so the take-or-pay language does not override it. The comment offers the 60-day/3-month-fee fallback as a negotiating position.
